text:
Character id: tonto

Aliases: Tonto

Appearances:
- page_id: 003_The_Metabarons_1_p01; note: addressed off-panel as storyteller
- page_id: 007_The_Metabarons_1_p05; note: named explicitly; identified as robot storyteller
- page_id: 019_The_Metabarons_1_p17; note: named; reports internal component failure

Relationships:
- character: the_metabaron; relation: servant; refers to him as 'master'
- character: lothar; relation: companion robot; storytelling partner

Witnessed facts:
- knows the Metabaron possesses a bionic ear and bionic lobes in the right half of his brain
- knows the Metabaron's absence duration to a precise standard-time measurement
- knows the origin story of the Metabaron caste back to great-great-grandfather Othon von Salza

Knowledge boundaries:
- narrates history as oral account; implies knowledge is secondhand or inherited
- exact limits of Tonto's first-person observation versus learned history are not defined

Important actions:
- page_id: 007_The_Metabarons_1_p05; action: agrees to narrate the full origin story of the Metabaron caste
- page_id: 019_The_Metabarons_1_p17; action: reports blowing an electro-emotion diode and activating auxiliary system mid-narration

Voice notes:
- speaks with exasperation toward Lothar; narrates history in an epic, sometimes sardonic register; breaks the fourth wall with comic malfunction asides

Character id: lothar

Aliases: Lothar

Appearances:
- page_id: 007_The_Metabarons_1_p05; note: named explicitly by Tonto; shown as eager listener

Relationships:
- character: tonto; relation: companion robot; story audience

Witnessed facts:
- heard Tonto describe the Meta-warrior mutilation customs just before p05

Knowledge boundaries:
- dependent on Tonto for historical knowledge of the Metabaron lineage

Important actions:
- page_id: 007_The_Metabarons_1_p05; action: presses Tonto to tell the full origin story of the Metabaron caste

Voice notes:
- enthusiastic, almost childlike fascination with the Metabaron's violent history; pushes narrative forward as a foil to Tonto

Character id: the_metabaron

Aliases: The Metabaron, meta-warrior

Appearances:
- page_id: 001_The_Metabarons_1_c01; note: cover figure, unnamed; bald, stern, associated with ornate sword and cybernetic elements
- page_id: 004_The_Metabarons_1_p02; note: described by Tonto; not physically present

Relationships:
- character: tonto; relation: master
- character: lothar; relation: master
- character: othon_von_salza; relation: great-great-grandson (implied through lineage narration)

Knowledge boundaries:
- absent at the time of the framing narrative; not directly observed on story pages

Important actions:
- page_id: 004_The_Metabarons_1_p02; note: his bionic augmentations are the narrative catalyst for Tonto's origin story

Voice notes:
- not directly heard speaking in this volume; known only through Tonto's description and cover imagery

Character id: othon_von_salza

Aliases: Othon von Salza

Appearances:
- page_id: 008_The_Metabarons_1_p06; note: named in ancestral narration; depicted or referenced in row of faces
- page_id: 012_The_Metabarons_1_p10; note: named; commits premature cutting discharge
- page_id: 015_The_Metabarons_1_p13; note: referenced as trapped, likely depicted as fallen armored figure
- page_id: 016_The_Metabarons_1_p14; note: rescue debate centers on him
- page_id: 018_The_Metabarons_1_p16; note: named; rebuked for pirate thinking; declared next baron
- page_id: 020_The_Metabarons_1_p18; note: target of Baron Berard's dagger attack
- page_id: 022_The_Metabarons_1_p20; note: named; receives the spirit and birthmark transfer from Berard
- page_id: 023_The_Metabarons_1_p22; note: recipient of Berard's completed transfer; marked with birthmark

Relationships:
- character: baron_berard; relation: father-in-law, master, predecessor baron; performs spirit transfer to Othon
- character: lady_edna; relation: wife; described as his mate by Berard
- character: bari; relation: son with Edna (referenced p06)
- character: the_metabaron; relation: great-great-grandfather

Witnessed facts:
- witnessed or caused industrial accident by triggering premature cutting discharge (p10)
- was trapped beneath a fallen stone block and rescued using the sacred glowing orb (p12–p15)
- witnessed Baron Berard declare him next baron and rebuke his pirate past (p16)
- received Berard's spirit, knowledge, and birthmark transfer before Berard's death (p20, p22)

Knowledge boundaries:
- at the start of the volume was considered to lack the willingness to sacrifice, per Berard's teaching (p20)
- no direct evidence of knowledge beyond what is depicted in these pages

Important actions:
- page_id: 012_The_Metabarons_1_p10; action: ignores father-in-law's instructions and triggers premature cut, causing industrial accident
- page_id: 020_The_Metabarons_1_p20; action: agrees to surrender to Berard's knowledge and accepts succession
- page_id: 022_The_Metabarons_1_p20; action: receives spirit and birthmark transfer from Berard; becomes new baron

Voice notes:
- speaks defiantly and impulsively in the accident scene; later speaks with emotional warmth toward Berard; accepts succession with formal address 'father'

Character id: lady_edna

Aliases: Lady Edna, Edna

Appearances:
- page_id: 008_The_Metabarons_1_p06; note: referenced as daughter of Baron Berard; described as beautiful and indomitable
- page_id: 011_The_Metabarons_1_p09; note: named; expected to perform precision cuts
- page_id: 016_The_Metabarons_1_p14; note: named; argues in favor of saving Othon
- page_id: 023_The_Metabarons_1_p22; note: addressed directly by dying Berard; admonished for showing emotion

Relationships:
- character: baron_berard; relation: daughter
- character: othon_von_salza; relation: wife; chosen mate per Berard's account (p20)
- character: bari; relation: mother (p06)

Witnessed facts:
- present at stone-cutting worksite (p09)
- present at rescue council debate and argued for Othon's rescue (p14)
- present when Berard performed the spirit transfer and died (p22/p23)

Knowledge boundaries:
- awareness of the sacred oil and its sensitivity is implied by the rescue debate context

Important actions:
- page_id: 016_The_Metabarons_1_p14; action: argues in council for saving Othon's life despite secrecy risk
- page_id: 023_The_Metabarons_1_p22; action: weeps at Berard's death; admonished by Berard for emotional weakness

Voice notes:
- speaks in favor of family over secrecy; emotional register contrasts with the warrior stoicism Berard demands

Character id: baron_berard

Aliases: Baron Berard, Berard, Baron Berard of Castaka

Appearances:
- page_id: 008_The_Metabarons_1_p06; note: named in narration as ruler of Marmola
- page_id: 011_The_Metabarons_1_p09; note: named in the worksite cutting scene as father/authority
- page_id: 012_The_Metabarons_1_p10; note: present as Othon's father-in-law during accident
- page_id: 015_The_Metabarons_1_p13; note: likely the grandfather figure pressuring Bari to let Othon die
- page_id: 018_The_Metabarons_1_p16; note: older white-haired elder giving final orders; orders visitors killed; declares Othon new baron
- page_id: 019_The_Metabarons_1_p17; note: described as heavy with gloom in his armory
- page_id: 020_The_Metabarons_1_p18; note: attacks Othon with a dagger; described as green-faced with white hair
- page_id: 021_The_Metabarons_1_p19; note: wins the duel against Othon
- page_id: 022_The_Metabarons_1_p20; note: explains duel lesson; performs spirit and birthmark transfer; prepares to die
- page_id: 023_The_Metabarons_1_p22; note: dies; instructs body be cast into the Great Azure Ocean
- page_id: 024_The_Metabarons_1_p23; note: referenced in narration; said to have died by stubbornly holding his breath

Relationships:
- character: lady_edna; relation: father
- character: othon_von_salza; relation: son-in-law; master; eventually accepts as worthy heir
- character: bari; relation: grandfather (implied via Edna being his daughter)
- character: the_metabaron; relation: great-great-grandfather

Witnessed facts:
- witnessed imperial visitors observe the sacred stone-loading secret (p09/p16)
- witnessed the glowing orb used to levitate the stone block; declared this a 'major technical revolution' via the authority figure's reaction (p16/p18)
- performed the spirit and birthmark transfer into Othon (p20/p22)
- predicted wars over sacred oil and refused to be part of that future (p23)

Knowledge boundaries:
- full custodian of the sacred oil secret and stone-loading method
- aware of imperial politics and the danger of exposure

Important actions:
- page_id: 018_The_Metabarons_1_p16; action: orders the imperial visitors killed; decrees Othon becomes new baron
- page_id: 020_The_Metabarons_1_p18; action: attacks Othon with a dagger in a formal duel
- page_id: 021_The_Metabarons_1_p19; action: wins the duel by deliberately accepting a shoulder wound as strategic sacrifice
- page_id: 022_The_Metabarons_1_p20; action: reveals birthmark; performs spirit and knowledge transfer into Othon
- page_id: 023_The_Metabarons_1_p22; action: dies; instructs body be cast into the Great Azure Ocean; warns of coming wars over sacred oil

Voice notes:
- commands with authority and finality; speaks in the idiom of honor, sacrifice, and warrior tradition; admonishes emotion as weakness; formal register with son-in-law shifts to paternal warmth only when acknowledging Othon's worth

Character id: bari

Aliases: Bari

Appearances:
- page_id: 008_The_Metabarons_1_p06; note: referenced as infant/son of Othon and Edna
- page_id: 011_The_Metabarons_1_p09; note: named; entrusted with clean cuts during marble operation
- page_id: 015_The_Metabarons_1_p13; note: likely the Bari confronting elders about Othon; identified as a warrior
- page_id: 016_The_Metabarons_1_p14; note: likely the younger silver-haired man who overrules his father in the council

Relationships:
- character: othon_von_salza; relation: child (Othon is her/his father)
- character: lady_edna; relation: child (Edna is mother)
- character: baron_berard; relation: grandchild (implied)

Witnessed facts:
- present at marble-cutting worksite (p09)
- present at council debate over rescuing Othon (p13/p14)

Knowledge boundaries:
- awareness of the sacred technology is implied; aware of what secrecy cost could be

Important actions:
- page_id: 015_The_Metabarons_1_p13; action: defies elder patriarch; insists Othon will live; accuses patriarch of prejudice over birth status
- page_id: 016_The_Metabarons_1_p14; action: overrules father in council vote to save Othon

Voice notes:
- passionate and confrontational in council; speaks in terms of love vs. hatred and lineage acceptance

Character id: the_techno_pope

Aliases: The Techno-Pope

Appearances:
- page_id: 008_The_Metabarons_1_p06; note: referenced; planning a new temple-bank requiring vast marble
- page_id: 009_The_Metabarons_1_p07; note: referenced; project scale escalates to requiring an entire mountain of marble

Relationships:
- character: imperial_merchants_guild; relation: employs or commissions them for marble acquisition

Knowledge boundaries:
- not present in person; known only through the ship crew's references

Important actions:
- page_id: 008_The_Metabarons_1_p06; action: commissions marble from Marmola for a new temple-bank, triggering the Guild ship's arrival

Voice notes:
- never speaks directly in this volume

Character id: hohenhole

Aliases: Hohenhole

Appearances:
- page_id: 011_The_Metabarons_1_p09; note: named; mentally distracted by songs during the cutting operation

Relationships:
- character: baron_berard; relation: team member under his command

Important actions:
- page_id: 011_The_Metabarons_1_p09; action: must be reminded to concentrate on the stone-cutting task

Voice notes:
- distracted register; must be redirected to focus

Character id: sire_barako

Aliases: Sire Barako

Appearances:
- page_id: 011_The_Metabarons_1_p09; note: named; seeks evaluation of his work during operation

Relationships:
- character: baron_berard; relation: team member under his command

Voice notes:
- asks 'how am I doing?' mid-operation

Character id: konrath

Aliases: Konrath

Appearances:
- page_id: 010_The_Metabarons_1_p08; note: named by off-panel voices; visually unconfirmed which figure is him

Witnessed facts:
- approached a significant white cubic structure in an alien landscape (p08)

Knowledge boundaries:
- receives contradictory orders; context suggests an ongoing operation already underway

Voice notes:
- addressed but not heard speaking

Character id: black_endoguard

Aliases: Black Endoguard

Appearances:
- page_id: 025_The_Metabarons_1_p24; note: named in narration as the group that delivers an unexpected betrayal

Relationships:
- character: imperial_house; relation: apparent allies or subordinates; their betrayal benefits the Imperial House

Important actions:
- page_id: 025_The_Metabarons_1_p24; action: betrays their side unexpectedly during the space battle over Marmola, contributing to the opposing fleet's defeat

Voice notes:
- not directly heard

Character id: castakan_warrior_last_stand

Aliases: Unknown Castakan Warrior, warrior of Castaka

Appearances:
- page_id: 027_The_Metabarons_1_p26; note: central action figure; self-identifies or is identified as 'a warrior of Castaka'

Relationships:
- character: castaka_lineage; relation: member or descendant of Castaka

Important actions:
- page_id: 027_The_Metabarons_1_p26; action: fights through multiple armored guards in a stairwell and crashes through a window to escape or advance

Voice notes:
- defiant; identifies by lineage rather than personal name

Character id: othon-von-salza

Aliases: Othon Von Salza, Baron of Castaka, Master Othon, the Baron

Appearances:
- volume: 2; pages: ['ic1', 'p01', 'p02', 'p03', 'p04', 'p05', 'p06', 'p07', 'p08', 'p09', 'p10', 'p11', 'p21', 'p25', 'p26']

Traits:
- White-haired, heavily armored warrior
- Former pirate who married into the Castaka clan
- Tactically precise; exploits environmental and anatomical vulnerabilities
- Emotionally stoic even during personal loss
- Physically bold — leads from the front
- Pragmatic negotiator; uses leverage coldly
- Deeply loyal to the fallen; personally retrieves bodies and honors death sites
- Initiator of cybernetic augmentation tradition in the lineage

Relationships:
- character: Edna; relation: Wife (deceased); notes: Married into the Castaka clan; mourned her at the column where she was disintegrated
- character: Baron Berard of Castaka; relation: Father-in-law (deceased); notes: Berard initially opposed Othon, then judged him worthy and transferred the family legacy to him
- character: Bari; relation: Son; notes: Broke Bari's legs to prevent him from fighting; reconciled after battle; later suppressed public alarm to protect Bari's honor
- character: Bari Didi; relation: Biological heir; notes: Fathered despite castration; confirmed as direct blood successor
- character: Konrath; relation: Subordinate / loyal companion (deceased); notes: Retrieved Konrath's body from the southern ruins after battle
- character: Hohenhole; relation: Lieutenant (fate unconfirmed); notes: Searched the northern battlefield for Hohenhole after the fighting ended
- character: Iku-Tta / Iku-Itta; relation: Trusted attendant / confidant; notes: Confided loneliness to Iku-Tta; Iku-Tta and daughters nursed him during recovery
- character: Tonto; relation: Descendant / addressee of lineage narrative; notes: Othon's exploits are recounted to Tonto as ancestral legend

Witnessed facts:
- Watched the clan expose the Epyphite secret to save him from the marble block
- Saw Baron Berard transfer the family legacy before dying
- Observed Edna walk out alone to confront the invaders
- Led the three-pronged counterattack against the endoguards
- Walked the valley battlefield covered in corpses in the aftermath
- Attended Oda's funerary bier and reconciled with Bari
- Negotiated directly with the imperial couple over Epyphite access
- Witnessed Bari bond with Shazam on Okhar
- Ambushed the green-skinned raiders in fog using a bow and terrain knowledge

Knowledge boundaries:
- Sole shared knowledge (with Bari) of the precise location / access method of the Epyphite — used as negotiating leverage
- Personally knows the terrain of the marble fortress on Okhar
- Knows the vulnerabilities of endoguard armor (tiny gaps exploitable with precise dagger strikes)

Important actions:
- action: Solo infiltration through enemy center; detail: Advanced armed only with a short dagger; killed approximately 1,500 endoguards by striking tiny gaps in their armor; source_pages: ['p04', 'p05']
- action: Broke Bari's legs; detail: Deliberately crippled Bari to prevent him joining the battle; source_pages: ['ic1', 'p02']
- action: Retrieved Konrath's body and honored Edna's death site; detail: Carried Konrath south through ruins; knelt at the column where Edna was disintegrated; source_pages: ['p07']
- action: Negotiated with the imperial couple; detail: Used exclusive Epyphite knowledge as leverage to secure revenue share, the planet Okhar, and Shazam for Bari; source_pages: ['p10', 'p11']
- action: Ambushed the Shazam raiders in fog; detail: Used bow and terrain knowledge; defeated them but suffered catastrophic groin/hip injuries; source_pages: ['p21', 'p24', 'p25']
- action: Founded metabaronic traditions; detail: Invested fortune in first metabaronic weapons and initiated cybernetic implant practice; received a multi-protonic pelvis; source_pages: ['p26']
- action: Fathered Bari Didi; detail: Despite castration, fathered a biological son, preserving direct blood succession; source_pages: ['p26']

Voice notes:
- Speaks in terms of warrior doctrine and ruthless tactical logic
- Emotionally restrained in dialogue even during grief or reconciliation
- In negotiations: calm, leveraged, never emotional

Character id: edna

Aliases: Edna, Edna of Castaka

Appearances:
- volume: 2; pages: ['ic1', 'p02', 'p07']

Traits:
- Daughter of Baron Berard of Castaka
- Deeply committed to clan honor
- Willing to sacrifice herself to defend the clan's reputation
- Armed and combative

Relationships:
- character: Baron Berard of Castaka; relation: Father (deceased)
- character: Othon Von Salza; relation: Husband
- character: Bari; relation: Son; notes: Bari declared he wanted to die like his mother

Witnessed facts:
- Saw her father transfer the family legacy to Othon before dying
- Was present during the battle over Marmola

Knowledge boundaries:
- Knew the Epyphite secret (implied by clan membership)

Important actions:
- action: Walked alone to confront the invading force; detail: Went out to defend clan honor against the invaders; was disintegrated at the base of a great column; source_pages: ['ic1', 'p02', 'p07']

Voice notes:
- Not directly quoted in surviving pages; described as acting from honor rather than orders
- Her death is framed by others as 'needless' but Bari views it as heroic

Character id: baron-berard-of-castaka

Aliases: Baron Berard of Castaka, Berard, the Baron

Appearances:
- volume: 2; pages: ['ic1']

Traits:
- Ruler of Marmola
- Initially suspicious of Othon; placed clan secrecy above Othon's life
- Eventually recognized Othon as a worthy successor
- Source of martial doctrine; his sayings are quoted by later commanders as authoritative

Relationships:
- character: Edna; relation: Daughter
- character: Othon Von Salza; relation: Son-in-law and successor
- character: Castaka clan; relation: Patriarch

Witnessed facts:
- Saw the clan vote to expose the Epyphite secret to save Othon
- Judged Othon's reaction and found him worthy

Knowledge boundaries:
- Sole guardian of the Epyphite secret before passing the legacy to Othon

Important actions:
- action: Opposed revealing Epyphite to save Othon; detail: Prioritized secrecy over Othon's life until the clan overruled him; source_pages: ['ic1']
- action: Transferred the family legacy to Othon; detail: Formally passed clan leadership and knowledge to Othon before dying; source_pages: ['ic1']

Voice notes:
- Quoted posthumously in battle: his sayings about total commitment to destroying the enemy are cited as authoritative military doctrine
- Direct speech not shown in surviving pages of this volume

Character id: bari

Aliases: Bari

Appearances:
- volume: 2; pages: ['ic1', 'p02', 'p08', 'p10', 'p11', 'p15', 'p16', 'p17', 'p19', 'p20', 'p23', 'p24', 'p25']

Traits:
- Young; emotionally volatile and impulsive
- Physically disabled: legs broken by his father, then later crippled in combat
- Equates death in battle with honor; initially suicidal in his idealism
- Capable of genuine remorse and reconciliation
- Deeply bonded to Shazam the horse
- Determined to fight despite physical limitations

Relationships:
- character: Othon Von Salza; relation: Father; notes: Condemned Othon as a coward for breaking his legs; reconciled and called him the noblest of the clan
- character: Edna; relation: Mother (deceased); notes: Viewed her death as heroic and wanted to emulate it
- character: Shazam; relation: Bonded companion / gifted horse; notes: Shazam became a source of renewed joy and life purpose for Bari
- character: Iku-Tta; relation: Attendant / stable-keeper
- character: Bari Didi; relation: Implied future identity or descendant (name appears as Othon's heir in p26 dialogue)

Witnessed facts:
- Was present at the battle on Marmola (prevented from fighting by broken legs)
- Witnessed his mother Edna's death or its immediate aftermath
- Attended Oda's funerary bier and reconciled with his father
- Was present at the Epyphite reservoir during negotiations
- Was publicly honored by the imperial couple on Marmola

Knowledge boundaries:
- Shares exclusive knowledge of Epyphite's location with Othon — cited as negotiating leverage
- Aware of the secret tunnels used in the battle

Important actions:
- action: Attempted to pursue the invaders despite broken legs; detail: Was physically stopped by his father; source_pages: ['ic1', 'p02']
- action: Broke down and reconciled with his father; detail: Embraced Othon, retracted his judgment of cowardice, called him the noblest of the clan; source_pages: ['p08']
- action: Bonded with Shazam; detail: Named the resurrected horse, fed it sugar, began riding it on Okhar; horse described as restoring his appetite for life; source_pages: ['p16']
- action: Pursued Shazam's thieves despite crippled legs; detail: Left before his father was informed; fought the green-skinned raiders; source_pages: ['p20', 'p23', 'p24']

Voice notes:
- Speaks in passionate, accusatory terms when in emotional distress
- Explicitly equates glorious death with honor; argues against pragmatic survival
- Voice softens to remorse and gratitude when reconciling with his father

Character id: konrath

Aliases: Konrath

Appearances:
- volume: 2; pages: ['p03', 'p04', 'p07']

Traits:
- Twin of Hohenhole
- Loyal companion to Othon
- Assigned the southern attack vector in the three-pronged battle plan
- Falls in battle

Relationships:
- character: Hohenhole; relation: Twin brother
- character: Othon Von Salza; relation: Commander / loyal companion; notes: Othon retrieved his body from the southern ruins as a mark of honor

Witnessed facts:
- Participated in the southern attack via secret tunnels against the endoguards

Knowledge boundaries:
- Knew the layout of the secret tunnels used in the southern assault

Important actions:
- action: Led the southern assault; detail: Tasked with using secret tunnels to keep endoguards compressed together; source_pages: ['p03']
- action: Died in battle; detail: Body recovered by Othon from the southern ruins; source_pages: ['p07']

Voice notes:
- Not directly quoted in surviving pages of this volume

Character id: hohenhole

Aliases: Hohenhole

Appearances:
- volume: 2; pages: ['p03', 'p04', 'p06']

Traits:
- Twin of Konrath
- Assigned the northern attack vector
- Fate unconfirmed: Othon searches for him in the northern battlefield but no resolution is shown

Relationships:
- character: Konrath; relation: Twin brother
- character: Othon Von Salza; relation: Lieutenant / subordinate; notes: Othon personally searched the northern battlefield for him

Witnessed facts:
- Led the northern assault; tasked with locking the enemy into hand-to-hand combat

Important actions:
- action: Led the northern assault; detail: Assigned half the men; ordered to engage endoguards at close range; source_pages: ['p03']
- action: Fate unknown; detail: Othon searches for him in the northern battlefield aftermath; no resolution shown in this volume; source_pages: ['p06']

Voice notes:
- Not directly quoted in surviving pages of this volume

Character id: oda

Aliases: Oda

Appearances:
- volume: 2; pages: ['p08']

Traits:
- Warrior who fulfilled their destiny by fighting fiercely to the end
- Spoken of in eulogistic terms; death described as entering 'silence, the soul of all things'

Relationships:
- character: Bari; relation: Associated with Bari's funerary mourning scene
- character: Othon Von Salza; relation: Member of the same fighting group or clan

Important actions:
- action: Fell in battle; detail: Described as having fought ferociously until the end; body laid on a raised funerary slab; source_pages: ['p08']

Voice notes:
- Not directly quoted; only referenced in memorial narration

Non-peer reason: Only memorial narration for a fallen Marmola warrior: no direct voice and no durable behavior beyond fighting fiercely and dying; useful as contextual funeral/battle lore for Othon and Bari, not as a scene persona.

Character id: tonto

Aliases: Tonto

Appearances:
- volume: 2; pages: ['p05', 'p15', 'p26']

Traits:
- Listens to accounts of the Metabaron lineage from a small floating narrator
- Treated familiarly by the narrator
- Addressed as a recipient of ancestral stories; implied to be a descendant or close associate of the Metabaron
- Present in the framing narrative throughout the volume

Relationships:
- character: Lothar; relation: Co-participant in the framing narrative / questioner
- character: Othon Von Salza; relation: Ancestor whose exploits are recounted to Tonto

Witnessed facts:
- Hears the recounting of Othon's solo endoguard kill feat
- Participates in the discussion of how Othon's castrated lineage produced an heir

Knowledge boundaries:
- Knowledge of the Metabaron lineage is mediated through the narrator's accounts, not direct experience

Voice notes:
- Not directly quoted at length in surviving pages; functions as an audience figure
- Offered 'ultra-coolant' as a drink by the narrator (p05)

Character id: lothar

Aliases: Lothar

Appearances:
- volume: 2; pages: ['p15', 'p26']

Traits:
- Skeptical and inquisitive; repeatedly asks whether promises were genuinely fulfilled
- Co-participant in the framing narrative with Tonto
- Asks naive questions about reproduction (corrected by another speaker on p26)

Relationships:
- character: Tonto; relation: Co-participant in framing narrative
- character: Othon Von Salza; relation: Learns of Othon's lineage through the narration

Witnessed facts:
- Hears confirmation that the family received a revenue share from Epyphite and inherited Okhar
- Hears the discussion of how the castrated Othon fathered an heir

Knowledge boundaries:
- Questions suggest limited prior knowledge of the lineage's history

Voice notes:
- Persistently skeptical: frames questions as 'but were they truly given what was promised?'
- Corrected when he implies Othon may have adopted rather than fathered an heir

Character id: iku-tta

Aliases: Iku-Tta, Iku-Itta

Appearances:
- volume: 2; pages: ['p17', 'p19', 'p20', 'p25']

Traits:
- Loyal attendant and confidant to Master Othon
- Associated with the stables / horse-keeping on Okhar
- Has two daughters who assist in nursing
- Trusted enough to hear Othon's private admissions of loneliness

Relationships:
- character: Othon Von Salza; relation: Trusted attendant / confidant
- character: Bari; relation: Aware of Bari's condition and welfare
- character: Iku-Tta's two daughters; relation: Father

Witnessed facts:

Character id: honorata

Appearances:

Traits:

- Last surviving member of the Von Salzas bloodline

- Emits hypnotic waves; Aghnar eventually learns to resist them [111_The_Metabarons_4_p22]
- Emotionally intense and decisive; takes command of rooms under threat
- Capable of maternal feeling but ruthlessly suppresses it in training context
- Severe disciplinarian; enforces emotional detachment and total-distrust doctrine
- Capable of bearing extreme physical hardship (mountain exile, eodactyl attack, birth mid-air)

Relationships:
- character: Othon von Salza; type: lover / father of her child; notes: Originally sent to seduce him by the Oiders; fell in love and defied orders; conceived Aghnar via blood ritual; permanently sterile after; reunited after seven years
- character: Aghnar; type: mother / trainer; notes: Raised him in seven-year exile at Anasirma; administered brutal Shabda-Oud training including corporal punishment and forced emotional cruelty; gave him the only kiss of his childhood after he defeated her in combat
- character: The Empress; type: patron who dispatched her; notes: The Empress sent Honorata to Okhar as a gift to Othon
- character: The Oiders; type: authority she defied; notes: Sent by Oiders to produce a perfect androgyne for succession plot; disobeyed out of love and bore a son instead
- character: Iku-Tta's daughters; type: non-peer enemies / captors; notes: the two daughters seized her in ninth month of pregnancy and threw themselves with her from the tower

Witnessed facts:
- Arrived on Okhar sent by the Empress and the Oiders [089_The_Metabarons_4_ic1]
- First encounter with Othon interrupted by his jealous servants [089_The_Metabarons_4_ic1]
- During a lunar eclipse told Othon she was the last of the Von Salzas and could not transmit the White Castaka birthmark [092_The_Metabarons_4_p03]
- Proposed blood-ritual conception as alternative to normal union [092_The_Metabarons_4_p03]
- Conceived Aghnar during a nervous-system-linked ritual; this left her permanently sterile [093_The_Metabarons_4_p04, 104_The_Metabarons_4_p15]
- In ninth month of pregnancy, seized by Iku-Tta's daughters and thrown from the tower [094_The_Metabarons_4_p05]
- Struck by an epiphyte dart during the fall; suspended in air by wind; gave birth between sky and ground [099_The_Metabarons_4_p10]
- Revealed the Oiders' succession conspiracy and her defiance; agreed to seven-year concealment plan [101_The_Metabarons_4_p12]
- Took Aghnar into exile at Anasirma — a sacred mountain forbidden for centuries [107_The_Metabarons_4_p18]
- Survived eodactyl attack and sheltered in crystal cave with Aghnar [108_The_Metabarons_4_p19]
- Ordered Aghnar at age five to kill his beloved toad companion as a lesson in duty over love [109_The_Metabarons_4_p20]
- Trained Aghnar with escalating weights every six months, daily combat, Shabda-Oud meditation, auto-hypnosis [110_The_Metabarons_4_p21, 111_The_Metabarons_4_p22]
- Administered corporal punishment including lashing Aghnar for shedding a single tear [110_The_Metabarons_4_p21]
- Was defeated by Aghnar in combat when he resisted her hypnotic waves; gave him the only kiss of his childhood [111_The_Metabarons_4_p22]
- Rode a trained eodactyl with Aghnar to the Castaka fortress on the eve of his seventh birthday [112_The_Metabarons_4_p23]
- Reunited with Othon after seven years [113_The_Metabarons_4_p24]
- Objected to the robo-killer trial as excessively lethal [114_The_Metabarons_4_p25]
- Was directly present and protesting during Aghnar's foot-crushing ordeal [119_The_Metabarons_4_p30]

Knowledge boundaries:

- Knew Aghnar's weightlessness was caused by the epiphyte penetrating the embryonic sac during her fall [103_The_Metabarons_4_p14]
- Knew she cannot transmit the White Castaka birthmark [092_The_Metabarons_4_p03]

- action: Proposed and enacted blood-ritual conception, accepting permanent sterility; source_refs: ['092_The_Metabarons_4_p03', '093_The_Metabarons_4_p04']
- action: Survived tower fall and mid-air birth; body carried suspended by epiphyte dart over forest; source_refs: ['099_The_Metabarons_4_p10']
- action: Raised Aghnar in seven-year exile at Anasirma, forging his pain tolerance and Shabda-Oud mastery; source_refs: ['107_The_Metabarons_4_p18', '108_The_Metabarons_4_p19', '109_The_Metabarons_4_p20', '110_The_Metabarons_4_p21', '111_The_Metabarons_4_p22', '112_The_Metabarons_4_p23']
- action: Presented Aghnar to Othon at the Castaka fortress for initiation; source_refs: ['112_The_Metabarons_4_p23', '113_The_Metabarons_4_p24']
- action: Protested Othon's killing attempt on infant Aghnar; revealed permanent sterility making Aghnar their only possible child; source_refs: ['104_The_Metabarons_4_p15']

Voice notes:
- Commands rooms decisively; combines cold doctrine with rare flashes of maternal feeling; frames duty as supreme over love; can be seductive and commanding; uses sharp, final declarations ('duty above love', 'you are a Castaka')

Character id: aghnar

Aliases: Aghnar, Yippi (name used in the crystal cave childhood scenes)

Appearances:
- description: Born weightless; white/silver hair (visible through armor); depicted as infant through childhood to near-adulthood in this volume; receives metal prosthetic feet after initiation ordeal, which increase his weight; source_refs: ['102_The_Metabarons_4_p13', '109_The_Metabarons_4_p20', '112_The_Metabarons_4_p23', '120_The_Metabarons_4_p31']

Traits:
- Permanently weightless from birth due to epiphyte installed in cells by dart strike on Honorata's embryonic sac [103_The_Metabarons_4_p14]
- Exceptional pain tolerance developed through Shabda-Oud training and auto-hypnosis [110_The_Metabarons_4_p21]
- Emotionally repressed; trained to distrust everyone including his mother [110_The_Metabarons_4_p21]
- Courageous; frames tests as opportunities to earn his father's pride [119_The_Metabarons_4_p30]
- Capable of resisting his mother's hypnotic waves [111_The_Metabarons_4_p22]
- Castaka blood through Othon; White Castaka birthmark lineage
- Matures from infancy to near-adulthood described as unusually rapid [110_The_Metabarons_4_p21]
- After initiation: metal prosthetic feet granting increased weight and superhuman power [120_The_Metabarons_4_p31]

Relationships:
- character: Othon von Salza; type: father; notes: Conceived via blood ritual; seeks father's approval; subjected to brutal trials by Othon; Othon vowed to die if Aghnar fails
- character: Honorata; type: mother / trainer; notes: Raised and trained in seven-year exile at Anasirma; received only one kiss from her in childhood (reward for defeating her in combat)
- character: Woolly toad companion; type: beloved animal (killed on order); notes: Large male woolly toad that learned a few human words from Aghnar; ordered killed by Honorata at Aghnar's age five as a lesson in duty over love [109_The_Metabarons_4_p20]

Witnessed facts:
- Named Aghnar after Iku-Tta's suicide, in a robot-staffed room [102_The_Metabarons_4_p13]
- Discovered to levitate; cause identified as the epiphyte in his cells from the dart strike on Honorata's embryonic sac [103_The_Metabarons_4_p14]
- Othon moved to kill him as physically unfit; Honorata defended him [104_The_Metabarons_4_p15]
- A physical defect affecting normal leg function or walking was observed and diagnosed [105_The_Metabarons_4_p16]
- An unnamed figure volunteered to train him in Shabda-Oud skills [105_The_Metabarons_4_p16]
- Raised in exile at Anasirma crystal cave for seven years [107_The_Metabarons_4_p18]
- Survived on woolly toads with Honorata in the cave [109_The_Metabarons_4_p20]
- At age five, ordered to kill his toad companion as a lesson in duty over love [109_The_Metabarons_4_p20]
- Trained with escalating weights added every six months, daily combat, Shabda-Oud meditation, auto-hypnosis for pain suppression [110_The_Metabarons_4_p21, 111_The_Metabarons_4_p22]
- Lashed by his mother for shedding a single tear [110_The_Metabarons_4_p21]
- Defeated Honorata in combat by resisting her hypnotic waves; received the only kiss of his childhood [111_The_Metabarons_4_p22]
- Traveled with Honorata to the Castaka fortress on the eve of his seventh birthday [112_The_Metabarons_4_p23]
- Faced the robo-killer: fought for over an hour, then triggered its self-destruct via the red chest button [114_The_Metabarons_4_p25, 118_The_Metabarons_4_p29]
- Judges disputed legitimacy due to his weightlessness but honored their prior oath and accepted him as future Metabaron [118_The_Metabarons_4_p29]
- Endured a voice-keyed foot-crushing capsule without yielding; device destroyed his feet [119_The_Metabarons_4_p30]
- Received metal prosthetic feet; gained increased weight and superhuman power [120_The_Metabarons_4_p31]
- Bodily mutilation established as a component of Metabaronic initiation through his experience [120_The_Metabarons_4_p31]

Knowledge boundaries:
- Trained in Shabda-Oud meditation and auto-hypnosis; masters pain suppression [110_The_Metabarons_4_p21]
- Has internalized total-distrust doctrine including distrust of his own mother [110_The_Metabarons_4_p21]
- Born as a son, not the mandated hermaphrodite; his sex was kept secret for seven years [101_The_Metabarons_4_p12]
- Not depicted as aware of the Oiders' succession plot or his intended nature as a hermaphrodite

Important actions:
- action: Tamed a ferocious Eodactyl without Honorata's help before initiation; source_refs: ['114_The_Metabarons_4_p25']
- action: Killed his beloved toad companion on Honorata's order as a lesson in duty over love; source_refs: ['109_The_Metabarons_4_p20']
- action: Defeated Honorata in combat and resisted her hypnotic waves; source_refs: ['111_The_Metabarons_4_p22']
- action: Triggered robo-killer self-destruct after over an hour of combat; accepted as future Metabaron; source_refs: ['118_The_Metabarons_4_p29']
- action: Endured foot-crushing capsule to full destruction of his feet without yielding; source_refs: ['119_The_Metabarons_4_p30']
- action: Received metal prosthetic feet, becoming heavier and gaining superhuman power; source_refs: ['120_The_Metabarons_4_p31']

Voice notes:
- Short, determined utterances; says 'I want to make my father proud'; voices the internalized doctrine 'trust no one, not even your mother'; expresses hatred during combat training

Character id: aghnar

Aliases: Aghnar, Kiowotai (possibly, as perceived by the Magon — unresolved), Kioka (possibly, as invoked by Magon creatures — unresolved)

Appearances:
- source: vol6_ic1; page: ic1; description: Recap: attacked Shabda-Oud assassins with epyphite-tipped prosthetics; linked power with Honorata in a telepathic duel against the Mother Superior; departed Okhar with Othon and vowed revenge.
- source: vol6_c01; page: c01; description: Cover figure: white-haired humanoid in black bodysuit with mechanical claw prosthetics on arms and legs, fighting a giant creature. May be symbolic rather than a literal scene.
- source: vol6_p03; page: p03; description: Younger silver-haired character inside the Metabunker; emotionally challenges Othon's announcement of imminent death; identified as his son.
- source: vol6_p04; page: p04; description: Refuses Othon's demand to kill him; visibly horrified and armed during the confrontation.
- source: vol6_p05; page: p05; description: Young figure hesitating with a blade; Othon fires at him to force combat engagement.
- source: vol6_p06; page: p06; description: Projects destructive energy from his eyes (mental/psychic powers); identified as 'son' by the standing speaker; described as paralyzed.
- source: vol6_p07; page: p07; description: Confronts the scarred armored Othon with a blade; intelligent enough to challenge the bomb-threat logic (notes no bomb in the brain).
- source: vol6_p08; page: p08; description: Shoots Othon in the head, completing the Castaka patricide initiation rite; remains beside the corpse in grief or exhaustion.
- source: vol6_p09; page: p09; description: Subject of the robot narrator's account: isolated ~10 years on Perdita, rejected all offered entertainment, preserved Othon's body in deep-freeze, surgically extracted and grafted Oko mini-bombs into himself.
- source: vol6_p10; page: p10; description: Man with metal feet who ventures outside on Perdita for recreation; shoots an ape-like creature with an epyphite dart and brings it home.
- source: vol6_p11; page: p11; description: Attributed by volume chronology as the one who names the ape creature; the silver-haired man with a metal foot who heals and names it in the visual narrative may be the robot narrator acting on his behalf — identity uncertain on this page.
- source: vol6_p15; page: p15; description: Silver-haired humanoid with extended metal claws fights through alien tribal creatures; invoked in Magon legend as 'little no-hair white ape.' (Identification with Kiowotai/Kioka is uncertain.)
- source: vol6_p16; page: p16; description: Captured by a giant creature; tears or blasts through the creature's head area in reversal.
- source: vol6_p17; page: p17; description: Airborne figure after defeating the giant creature; Magon creatures below invoke 'Kioka' and speak of departure to the Diamond Planet.
- source: vol6_p18; page: p18; description: Mentioned only: eighteenth birthday serves as the time marker for the spy-needle signal's arrival.
- source: vol6_p19; page: p19; description: Inside spacecraft; learns Shabda-Oud have 7 cetacyborgs (6 guarding the comet, 1 away on a covert mission); devises Trojan-horse plan using the Magon; explicitly ties all strategy to avenging his mother; plans to become patriarch of the Magon proto-civilization.
- source: vol6_p20; page: p20; description: Loads Magon apes into the Metabunker with a false promise of passage to the Diamond Planet; apes are rendered comatose by heat-immunizing injection and jettisoned as feed to lure the seventh cetacyborg.
- source: vol6_p21; page: p21; description: Infiltrates the exterior and interior of the seventh cetacyborg alone in an armored space suit.
- source: vol6_p22; page: p22; description: Pale-haired armored attacker: shoots a Shabda-Oud sister and uses mental coercion to force the others to reveal their secret destination; described by an off-panel speaker as having turned the cetacyborg into a Trojan horse.
- source: vol6_p23; page: p23; description: Learns of Oda Capricious and the Shabda-Oud bloodline prophecy via intelligence gathered from the coerced sisters; reacts intensely to her holovid; concludes seduction is necessary.
- source: vol6_p24; page: p24; description: Vows to possess Oda even at the cost of his life; orders crew to stay behind and avoid raising alarm; takes a small moto-craft toward Amadis on Baggadathi.

Relationships:
- character: Othon; type: Father (deceased — killed by Aghnar); notes: Forced into patricide duel; killed him to complete the Castaka initiation. Sources: vol6_p04–vol6_p08.
- character: Honorata; type: Mother (deceased — annihilated with Okhar); notes: All revenge actions explicitly dedicated to avenging her. Sources: vol6_ic1, vol6_p04, vol6_p19.
- character: Robot Narrator; type: Guardian/caretaker during Perdita isolation; notes: Assigned by Othon to keep Aghnar occupied during the ten-year wait. Source: vol6_p09.
- character: Lothar; type: Robot companion/servant; notes: Present during isolation and medical scenes. Sources: vol6_p09, vol6_p18.
- character: Tonto; type: Robot surgical assistant; notes: Assists with medical procedures. Sources: vol6_p09, vol6_p18.
- character: The Ape Companion; type: Companion; rescued and named by Aghnar or his robot; notes: Foundation of his relationship with the Magon proto-civilization. Sources: vol6_p10, vol6_p11.
- character: Oda Capricious; type: Target of pursuit and desire; notes: Becomes intensely captivated by her holovid; resolved to win her. Sources: vol6_p23, vol6_p24.
- character: Shabda-Oud; type: Primary enemies; notes: Fought them in recap; now plots revenge and a Trojan-horse infiltration of their forces. Sources: vol6_ic1, vol6_p19, vol6_p22.

Witnessed facts:
- Watched Okhar and Honorata destroyed from orbit (vol6_ic1)
- Present when Othon revealed the spy-needle plan and his own imminent death (vol6_p03)
- Killed Othon with a shot to the head (vol6_p08)
- Spent approximately ten years in isolation on Planet Perdita tended only by robots (vol6_p09)
- Extracted Oko mini-bombs from Othon's corpse and grafted them into his own body (vol6_p09)
- Received the long-awaited spy-needle signal on his eighteenth birthday (vol6_p18)
- Learned the Shabda-Oud have 7 cetacyborgs total — 6 guarding the comet, 1 on a covert mission to the blue solar system of Beta-Kuntri (vol6_p19)
- Learned of the Shabda-Oud prophecy: his bloodline united with Oda Capricious would produce a supreme being capable of dethroning Janus-Jana (vol6_p23)
- Saw Oda Capricious via holovid (vol6_p23)

Knowledge boundaries:
- Knows the Shabda-Oud comet is guarded by 6 cetacyborgs with a 7th currently absent on a covert mission (vol6_p19)
- Knows his bloodline is tied to a Shabda-Oud prophecy involving Oda and a supreme being capable of dethroning Janus-Jana (vol6_p23)
- Knows Oda's marriage condition is an extinct blue rose — said to have been gone for 30,000 years (vol6_p23)
- Does not yet know how to fulfill the blue-rose condition (unresolved at volume end)
- Does not yet know Oda personally — only has seen her via holovid (vol6_p23)

Important actions:
- Defeated Shabda-Oud assassins with epyphite-tipped prosthetics; linked power with Honorata in telepathic duel against the Mother Superior (vol6_ic1)
- Killed Othon by shooting him in the head, completing the Castaka patricide initiation (vol6_p08)
- Performed prolonged surgery to extract Oko mini-bombs from Othon's corpse and implant them in himself (vol6_p09)
- Captured and rescued a rational ape-like creature on Perdita; named it (vol6_p10, vol6_p11 — attribution partially uncertain)
- Fought through Magon tribal creatures and defeated the Patriarch, fulfilling the Magon prophecy (vol6_p15–vol6_p17)
- Loaded Magon apes into the Metabunker under false pretenses; expelled them as feed to lure the seventh cetacyborg (vol6_p20)
- Infiltrated the seventh cetacyborg alone in vacuum, ambushed and mentally coerced the Shabda-Oud sisters inside (vol6_p21, vol6_p22)
- Set course for Baggadathi/Amadis alone in a small moto-craft to pursue Oda Capricious (vol6_p24)

Voice notes:
- Speaks with intense emotional investment when discussing revenge or family — 'what game are you playing?' (vol6_p03)
- Commands followers with authority and brevity; allows no dissent (vol6_p22, vol6_p24)
- Inwardly scorns rival suitors' ostentation (vol6_p24)

Character id: othon

Appearances:

- source: vol6_p06; page: p06; description: Standing figure who praises Aghnar's use of mental powers but immediately warns the fight is not over because Aghnar is paralyzed.
- source: vol6_p07; page: p07; description: Scarred, restrained armored man; threatens Oko mini-bomb detonation to prevent ordinary attack; demands to be killed to pass into 'true life'; praises Aghnar's intelligence when Aghnar identifies the brain-bomb exception.
- source: vol6_p08; page: p08; description: Shot in the head by Aghnar; body preserved in deep-freeze afterward.
- source: vol6_p09; page: p09; description: Mentioned only: his prior orders assigned the robot to keep Aghnar occupied during the wait; his corpse is on the operating table from which the Oko mini-bombs are extracted.

Relationships:

- character: Robot Narrator; type: Robot under his command; notes: Gave standing orders to keep Aghnar occupied during the ten-year wait. Source: vol6_p09.

Witnessed facts:
- Destroyed the Cetacyborg by infiltrating it from within — a viral-infiltration tactic — fatally contaminating himself (vol6_ic1)
- Witnessed Honorata and Okhar destroyed from orbit (vol6_ic1)
- Knew his blood was contaminated by Cetacyborg gases with only days to live (vol6_p03)

Knowledge boundaries:
- Knew the spy-needles would take ten years to return signals (vol6_p03)
- Knew Planet Perdita and its ecology well enough to summarize it (vol6_p02)
- Knew the Castaka tradition requiring patricide as Metabaron initiation (vol6_p04, vol6_p08)

Important actions:
- Infiltrated and destroyed the Cetacyborg from within using viral tactics, fatally contaminating himself in the process (vol6_ic1)
- Dispatched spy-needles across the universe before arriving on Perdita (vol6_p03)
- Ordered a ten-year concealment on Perdita and assigned the robot to maintain Aghnar (vol6_p03, vol6_p09)
- Forced Aghnar into a duel at gunpoint; demanded patricide as Castaka initiation (vol6_p04, vol6_p05)
- Revealed Oko mini-bomb implants as a tactical deterrent against ordinary attack (vol6_p07)
- Died when Aghnar shot him in the head (vol6_p08)

Voice notes:
- Commands with controlled aggression; willing to fire on his own son to force development (vol6_p05)
- Speaks philosophically about death as 'true life' — not resignation but desire (vol6_p07)
- Terse inventory style when describing the external world (vol6_p02)

Character id: aghnar

Aliases: Aghnar, the Metabaron

Appearances:
- volume: 7; pages: ['ic1 (recap)', 'p01', 'p04', 'p05', 'p06', 'p07', 'p08', 'p11', 'p12', 'p13', 'p14', 'p19', 'p20', 'p21', 'p23', 'p24', 'p25', 'p26', 'p27']

Traits:
- Driven by vengeance for Othon and Honorata above all else
- Tactically brilliant — employs deception, psychic disguise, mind-control, and concealed weapons simultaneously
- Stoic about physical suffering; frames spiritual integrity as inviolable even while losing a limb
- Romantically devoted to Oda from first sight (holovid); imagines escaping the Metabaron lineage to live as an ordinary family
- Willing to weaponize his own body — sacrifices arm as an internal bomb
- Holds himself to a Metabaron code that demands certain trials be faced alone, though he ultimately accepts Oda's help
- Cybernetic enhancements including mechanical limbs and the ability to project eye-beams; can hover

Relationships:
- character: Othon; type: son; notes: Killed Othon in sanctioned single combat at Othon's explicit demand; motivated ever after to avenge him
- character: Honorata; type: figure to avenge; notes: Honorata's fate is the original driving wound of his revenge arc; exact relationship not specified in vol 7 pages
- character: Oda; type: beloved / ally / mind's-shadow partner; notes: Fell in love via holovid; recruited her as willing co-conspirator; their mind's-shadow union during the Elders' assault is described as making them 'united forever'
- character: Kiowata; type: companion; notes: Saved and befriended the speaking Magon; Kiowata aided his cetacyborg mission
- character: Tonto; type: robot retainer; notes: Tonto serves the household and can perform surgery at the Metabunker; Aghnar's last hope for Oda's recovery
- character: Jejoh; type: enemy / destroyed by Aghnar; notes: Baited Jejoh into biting off his arm; the arm's concealed mini-bombs destroyed Jejoh from within

Witnessed facts:
- Watched Othon die from cetacyborg-released poison gas before killing him in combat (vol 7 ic1)
- Captured three Shabda-Oud pilots and learned their mission to abduct Oda for her genetics (vol 7 ic1)
- Saw a holovid of Oda and fell in love immediately (vol 7 ic1)
- Killed a Shabda-Oud priestess and constructed a psy-cloak from her identity to infiltrate the lair (vol 7 p11/p12)
- Passed the multi-layer biological, brainwave, and infra-conscious identity scan using psycho-mimetic training (vol 7 p13/p14)
- Saw Oda subjected to the witches' forced reproductive ritual (vol 7 p17)
- Provoked Jejoh to bite off his arm knowing the limb was loaded with mini-bombs (vol 7 p21)
- Witnessed the Shabda-Oud witches collapse after Jejoh's destruction (vol 7 p23)
- Survived the Elders' psychic assault through mind's-shadow union with Oda (vol 7 p25)
- Saw Oda left mentally devastated after the battle; carried her toward the Metabunker (vol 7 p27)

Knowledge boundaries:
- Does not know the Shabda-Oud cetacyborgs' secret weakness — Tonto warns this knowledge may die with the last surviving witch (vol 7 p27)
- Does not know how to bypass the cetacyborg blockade at the volume's end, though he reasons they must have a weak point (vol 7 p27)

Important actions:
- Killed father Othon in single combat to become a worthy avenger (vol 7 ic1)
- Defeated the Magon leader and fulfilled the Diamond Planet prophecy with Kiowata (vol 7 ic1)
- Traveled unarmed to Amadis, concealed Metabaron identity, competed in courtship trial, won Oda's blue-rose test (vol 7 p01–p05)
- Rejected the offered kingdom and took only Oda, precipitating the king's armed response (vol 7 p05)
- Escaped Amadis with Oda after her suicide-threat standoff with her father (vol 7 p06)
- Murdered a Shabda-Oud priestess and built a psy-cloak disguise from her identity (vol 7 p11)
- Used psychic mind-control to dominate two pilots en route to the ice asteroid (vol 7 p11/p12)
- Delivered Oda to the witches as a deliberate trap while disguised as a priestess (vol 7 p14/p15)
- Sacrificed his own arm — loaded with mini-bombs — by provoking Jejoh to consume it; destroyed Jejoh from within (vol 7 p21)
- Merged psychic energy with Oda in a mind's-shadow union to survive the Elders' final assault (vol 7 p25)
- Declared vengeance for Othon and Honorata achieved; expressed intent to cease being a Metabaron (vol 7 p26)
- Carrying Oda one-armed through a cetacyborg blockade toward the Metabunker at volume's end (vol 7 p27)

Voice notes:
- Internally: 'No one must learn I am the Metabaron until my vengeance is fulfilled' — restrains himself from attacking suitors openly at Amadis (vol 7 p01)
- To Oda: 'I no longer want you to remain a princess, and I no longer want to remain an assassin — I don't want our son to become a Metabaron' (vol 7 p08)
- After losing his arm: 'Only the stump hurts — my spirit cannot be wounded' (vol 7 p24)
- After Jejoh's destruction: declares Othon and Honorata avenged and that this moment should end his life as a Metabaron (vol 7 p26)
- To Oda during approach to the lair: plans to stage her as a bound captive and imagines they will flee to a distant planet afterward to live as an ordinary family (vol 7 p07)

Character id: oda

Aliases: Oda, Princess Oda, Oda the Capricious

Appearances:
- volume: 7; pages: ['ic1 (recap)', 'p02', 'p04', 'p05', 'p06', 'p07', 'p08', 'p14', 'p15', 'p16', 'p17', 'p19', 'p23', 'p24', 'p25', 'p26', 'p27']

- Repeatedly: 'That is not the blue rose I want' — dismisses every substitute offering (vol 7 p02, p03)

Character id: zaran-krleza

- Believed dead or extinct for approximately 5,000 years before Steelhead found him

Relationships:
- target: Steelhead / Melmoth; nature: Agreed to surgical fusion of his surviving head with Steelhead's body; both prior egos dissolved to produce Melmoth; source_refs: ['291_The_Metabarons_11_p14', '292_The_Metabarons_11_p15']

Witnessed facts:

Knowledge boundaries:
- Cannot pursue physical love — lacks a body; substitutes verbal/spiritual love
- Poetry still survives within his mind even without a body (p13)

Important actions:
- Survived 5,000 years as a preserved disembodied head by sacrificing the rest of his body to keep his soul alive (p13)

Voice notes:

- Frames entry requirements as a soul trial, not a strength test: 'I want to judge your soul' (p08–p09)
- Philosophy of love: verbal and spiritual love over carnal — regrets lack of body but does not regret the sacrifice (p13)

- Dona Vicenta, close to death from tuberculosis, is told only one of her twins can be born.

- Aghora waits three years for an Imperial Court assignment, but none comes.

- Aghora heads to the Golden Planet to learn why no one has called for the Metabaron's aid.

Volume: 1

Title: The Stonecutters

Chronology:
- FRAME: Tonto and Lothar, two robots aboard the metabunker spacecraft, open a storytelling exchange; Lothar demands the origin story of the Metabaron caste and Tonto reluctantly agrees.
- BACKSTORY BEGINS: Tonto identifies Othon von Salza, a former intergalactic pirate, as the Metabaron's great-great-grandfather.
- Othon wins Lady Edna's hand; Edna is the daughter of Baron Berard, undisputed ruler of Marmola and Castaka in the Philorian system; they produce one son, Bari.
- An Imperial Merchants Guild cargo ship arrives at Marmola on behalf of the Techno-Pope, who requires vast quantities of marble for a new temple-bank.
- The ship's crew observe that the Marmolans cut stone manually with hyperlaser tools and load cargo by a secret method: after a feasting ritual the visitors wake from drunkenness to find the hold already full.
- Baron Berard's team (including Edna, Bari, Hohenhole, and Sire Barako) performs a precision marble-cutting operation under the observation of imperial visitors.
- Othon ignores his father-in-law's timing instructions and triggers a premature cutting discharge; a massive stone block falls and traps him beneath the rubble.
- Elders debate whether to use their secret resource to save Othon, warning that exposure to the imperial visitors would end galactic peace.
- The council votes to save Othon, overruling the elder patriarch; a figure uses a small glowing orb to levitate the stone block; the operator collapses from the effort.
- An imperial authority witnessing the event declares it the greatest technical revolution of the century.
- Baron Berard orders the visitors killed and commands that they be given their marble; he decrees Othon will become the new baron and must swear loyalty to the Empire, rebuking Othon for thinking like a pirate.
- Baron Berard initiates a duel against Othon using a short dagger revered as an ancient Terra Prima weapon; Berard wins, having deliberately accepted a shoulder wound as a strategic sacrifice.
- Berard explains to Othon that victory requires the willingness to sacrifice; he formally accepts Othon as his worthy heir and his daughter's chosen mate.
- Berard performs a spirit and birthmark transfer, passing his lineage mark and knowledge into Othon, then bids farewell and prepares to die.
- Berard dies after predicting that wars of conquest over the planet's sacred oil will erupt across the galaxy; he instructs his body be cast into the Great Azure Ocean.
- Ten days after Berard's death, ships from multiple armed factions converge on Marmola and a massive space battle erupts.
- The Imperial House deploys gigantic battleships and crushes the rival fleets; the Black Endoguard delivers an unexpected betrayal that proves decisive.
- Imperial forces besiege the Castaka fortress; roughly 150 traditional defenders face approximately 1,500 heavily armed attackers.
- The defenders reject a surrender offer on grounds of honor and warrior oath; close-quarters melee erupts in the fortress hall.
- A warrior of Castaka cuts through multiple guards in a stairwell and crashes through a window; the volume ends at a cliffhanger with the next episode titled 'The Last Stand.'

Major events:
- Tonto narrates the origin of the Metabaron caste to Lothar, establishing the volume's storytelling frame aboard the metabunker.
- An Imperial Merchants Guild ship arrives at Marmola to collect marble for the Techno-Pope's temple-bank and inadvertently witnesses the Marmolans' secret sacred technology.
- Othon's industrial accident traps him under rubble, forcing the Castakan elders to choose between secrecy and family loyalty.
- The family council votes to save Othon; a glowing orb is used to levitate the stone block, exposing the sacred technology to imperial witnesses.
- Baron Berard declares the discovery a major technical revolution, orders the witnesses killed, and names Othon the next baron.
- Baron Berard duels Othon, deliberately accepts a wound to demonstrate sacrifice, then performs the spirit and birthmark transfer before dying.
- Ten days after Berard's death, a multi-faction space war erupts over Marmola; the Imperial House wins and the Black Endoguard betrays one side.
- The Castaka fortress is besieged; outnumbered defenders choose honorable death over surrender and the volume ends mid-battle.

Recurring motifs:
- Hereditary bodily mutilation and cybernetic augmentation as warrior initiation: the father destroys the son's ear and part of the right brain, then replaces them with bionics.
- Sacrifice and deliberate self-harm as the defining virtue of the Metabaron lineage.
- Secrecy as survival: the sacred oil and the stone-loading method are protected at any cost, including killing witnesses.
- Spirit and knowledge transferred physically from father to successor across generations, marked by a birthmark.
- Stoicism and suppression of emotion enforced as warrior identity; even a single tear is noted as a minor failure.
- Industrial labor (stone cutting) as a surface concealing sacred and dangerous hidden technology.
- The tension between imperial loyalty and clan secrecy.
- Honorable death in battle as preferable to survival through surrender or treachery.

Lore laws:
- Meta-warrior initiation is hereditary: the father deliberately destroys the son's right ear and part of the right brain, which are then replaced with bionic components.
- The Metabaron lineage is transmitted through a spirit and birthmark transfer from the dying patriarch to his chosen successor.
- Stoicism during initiation is culturally mandatory; a single shed tear is acknowledged as a minor failure against the ideal.
- The sacred oil of Marmola is an extraordinarily powerful substance even in tiny quantities; its existence is a state secret considered worth killing to conceal.
- The Marmolans load cargo onto visiting ships by a secret method performed while visitors sleep after a feast; they would rather die than reveal the technique.
- Ancient weapons from Terra Prima are revered above modern arms within Castakan warrior culture.
- Castakan warriors are oath-bound to the Empire and regard treachery as contemptible.
- An honorable death in battle is preferable to survival through surrender, according to the Castakan warrior code.
- A titled rank of baron exists within the ruling hierarchy of Marmola and Castaka, subject to imperial oath and formal succession.

Locations:
- The metabunker — an impregnable fortress within a bustling city-shaft; setting for the robot framing narrative; contains a large faceted object suspended in a glowing sphere at its heart.
- Marmola — a gigantic marble-producing world in the Philorian system; almost entirely stone with one small fertile valley; primary setting of the volume's flashback.
- Castaka — the fortress-valley on Marmola and seat of Baron Berard's rule; also described as a wealthy imperial center and 'planet of gold,' suggesting the name covers both the local fortress and a broader domain.
- Space above Marmola — site of the multi-faction space battle that erupts ten days after Berard's death.
- The Great Azure Ocean — a named body of water designated by Berard for his funerary disposal.
- The Castaka fortress hall — interior site of the final siege and last-stand melee at the volume's cliffhanger ending.

Open uncertainties:
- The exact nature and properties of the sacred oil — its origin, how it is produced, and how it relates to the glowing orb used to levitate the stone block — are not explained in this volume.
- The precise mechanism of the spirit and birthmark transfer is not described beyond that it is performed between elder and successor and leaves a physical mark.
- The identity of the figure who uses the glowing orb and collapses is not explicitly confirmed.
- The identity and function of the large faceted object suspended in a glowing sphere inside the metabunker are never explained.
- Whether the Castakan warrior who crashes through the window at the volume's end survives, and the outcome of the last stand, are unresolved.
- The exact content of the secret the Marmolans fear exposing to the Empire beyond involving the sacred oil and stone-loading method is not fully defined.
- The nature of the substance called 'lupium' mentioned briefly during the rescue debate is unclear.
- Several unnamed elders and attendants present at key council and duel scenes are never identified.

Volume: 2

Title: The Last Stand

Chronology:
- Recap: Othon Von Salza marries Edna (daughter of Baron Berard of Castaka) on Marmola; they have son Bari; Berard passes the family legacy to Othon before dying.
- The Castaka clan's secret anti-gravity oil Epyphite is exposed to the Imperial Merchants Guild during a crisis; a fleet battle erupts over Marmola; the black endoguards defect from the Empire and win.
- Othon breaks Bari's legs to stop him fighting; Edna goes alone to confront the invaders to defend clan honor and is disintegrated at the base of a great column.
- An armored speaker publicly denounces imperial generals as treacherous before the guards; the guards open fire.
- Othon organizes a three-pronged counterattack: Hohenhole attacks north, Konrath attacks south via secret tunnels, Othon infiltrates the enemy center alone with only a short dagger.
- Othon kills approximately 1,500 endoguards by exploiting tiny gaps in their supposedly impenetrable armor — a feat later recounted as a legendary ancestral exploit to Tonto.
- In the aftermath Othon searches the northern battlefield for Hohenhole, carries Konrath's body south through the ruins, and mourns Edna at the column where she was disintegrated.
- Oda falls in battle; Bari, wounded and bedridden, condemns his father as a coward then breaks down and asks forgiveness; father and son reconcile.
- News of Othon's deeds spreads galaxy-wide via interstellar spies; Othon is recognized as the new Baron of Castaka.
- One week later the imperial couple arrives at Marmola in their golden vessel with a purple Endoguard; Othon and Bari are publicly honored.
- In private negotiations Othon uses exclusive knowledge of the Epyphite's location as leverage; he warns that coercion alone would take years and demands terms.
- Othon secures a revenue share from Epyphite sales (founding the Metabarons' great fortune) and inherits the world of Okhar in the Diamond Constellation, where the Castaka fortress is rebuilt stone by stone.
- As an additional gift for Bari, Othon obtains Shazam — a white horse from a breed extinct for 20,000 years, recreated by imperial techno-scientists at a cost of 100 tons of gold.
- On Okhar Bari bonds with Shazam and enters a happier phase of life; Othon, now Master Othon, confides loneliness to attendant Iku-Tta.
- An armed raiding party (Ulkran, Wulthor, Tokkar, Bargoth) uses a paleo-compass and a marble disintegrator to breach the fortress on Okhar and steals Shazam using synthetic mare essence.
- Bari pursues the thieves despite his crippled legs; Othon is alerted by a servant, suppresses a public alarm to protect Bari's honor, and dons his own armor.
- Othon ambushes the raiders in dense fog exploiting terrain knowledge and a bow; Bari also fights the green-skinned raiders; Othon suffers catastrophic injury to his groin and hips.
- Shazam carries the gravely wounded Othon back to his palace; Iku-Tta and his two daughters nurse Othon through months of delirious recovery.
- Recovering, Othon invests his fortune in developing the first metabaronic weapons and begins the lineage tradition of cybernetic implants, including a multi-protonic pelvis.
- Despite his castration, Othon fathers a biological son, Bari Didi, ensuring direct blood succession.
- Volume closes with a teaser for the next episode: the knighting of Othon.

Major events:
- Battle of Marmola: the black endoguards defect from the Empire and win the fleet battle over control of the Epyphite.
- Edna's death: she confronts the invading force alone to defend clan honor and is disintegrated at the base of a column.
- Othon's solo infiltration: armed with only a short dagger, Othon kills approximately 1,500 endoguards by exploiting tiny gaps in their armor, becoming a founding legend of the Metabaron lineage.
- Post-battle mourning and reconciliation: Othon recovers Konrath's body, honors Edna's death site, and reconciles with a remorseful Bari over Oda's funeral bier.
- Empire-Castaka negotiations: Othon leverages exclusive knowledge of the Epyphite to extract a revenue share, the planet Okhar, and the gift of Shazam for Bari.
- Theft of Shazam: an armed raiding party breaches the marble fortress on Okhar and steals the resurrected horse using synthetic mare essence.
- Othon's castration: hunting the raiders in fog, Othon defeats them but suffers catastrophic groin and hip injuries; Shazam carries him home.
- Founding of the metabaronic tradition: Othon creates the first metabaronic weapons and initiates the family practice of cybernetic body augmentation.
- Succession confirmed: despite castration, Othon fathers biological heir Bari Didi, preserving the bloodline.

Recurring motifs:
- Father-son conflict, physical punishment, and reconciliation: Othon breaks Bari's legs; Bari condemns then forgives his father; Othon suppresses alarm to shield Bari's reputation.
- Physical mutilation as dynastic turning point: Bari's broken legs and Othon's castration each reshape the lineage's future.
- Honor versus pragmatism: characters openly contest whether glorious death, tactical deception, or survival best fulfills the warrior code.
- Tribute to the fallen: Othon personally retrieves Konrath's body and mourns at Edna's death site, framing loyalty to the dead as sacred duty.
- Ancestral exploit as oral legend: Othon's dagger feat is retold in the framing narrative to Tonto, establishing the series' storytelling frame.
- Restoration of the extinct at extreme cost: Shazam the resurrected horse and Othon's cybernetic pelvis both represent enormous expenditure to recover what was destroyed.
- Secrecy as power: the Epyphite secret, Bari's shame, and the fogbound raid all hinge on controlling what others know.

Lore laws:
- Epyphite is a sacred anti-gravity oil found deep beneath Marmola, described as the planet's sacred blood; the Castakas revered and guarded it for thousands of years before its exposure to the Empire.
- Endoguards are a military force with allegedly impenetrable armor; their only vulnerability is tiny gaps between plates, exploitable with precise close-range dagger strikes.
- The black endoguards defected from the Empire during the Marmola battle and fought on the Castaka side.
- Horses have been extinct for 20,000 years since the Sixth World War; the Imperial Palace maintains a genetic museum from which extinct species can be recreated by techno-scientists — Shazam cost 100 tons of gold.
- A paleo-compass can locate marble structures at range; a marble disintegrator can breach marble barriers.
- Synthetic mare essence, reproduced by technologists, can calm and guide a horse even after millennia of extinction.
- Othon Von Salza founded two defining traditions of the Metabaron lineage: development of specialized metabaronic weapons and the practice of cybernetic body augmentation, exemplified by his multi-protonic pelvis.
- The passage to the Epyphite reservoir beneath Marmola was carved by the Castakas thousands of years ago.
- The Metabarons' immense fortune originates from a negotiated percentage of Epyphite sale proceeds granted by the Empire.
- Warrior doctrine attributed to 'the Baron' holds that true valor transcends both triumph and defeat, and that tactical deception is acceptable in service of victory.

Locations:
- Marmola — the marble planet, homeworld of the Castaka clan, site of the Epyphite reservoir and the fleet battle.
- Castaka domain on Marmola — the family's stronghold and quarrying territory.
- Space above Marmola — site of the fleet battle between the Empire and the black endoguards.
- Epyphite reservoir — a vast subterranean cavern beneath Marmola, accessed via a passage carved by the Castakas thousands of years ago; described as a luminous, ocean-like expanse.
- Valley battlefield on Marmola — post-battle aftermath zone where Othon searches for Hohenhole and retrieves Konrath's body.
- Okhar — a fertile planet in the Diamond Constellation granted to Othon by the Empire; the Castaka fortress was transferred and rebuilt there.
- Marble fortress on Okhar — the relocated Castaka stronghold; breached by raiders using a paleo-compass and marble disintegrator.
- Golden imperial vessel — the distinctive ship used by the imperial couple to travel to Marmola for negotiations.
- Framing narrative setting — an unspecified interior where a small floating narrator recounts Othon's history to Tonto and Lothar.

Open uncertainties:
- Hohenhole's ultimate fate after the battle is not confirmed; Othon searches for him in the northern battlefield but no resolution is shown within the volume.
- The exact identities of the two unnamed figures speaking in the imperial context (p09 top panel) are not stated on the page.
- Whether the raiding party that stole Shazam acted independently or at someone's behest is never established.
- The nature of the green-skinned raiders — distinct species, augmented humans, or fighters with unusual coloring — is not explained.
- The method by which the castrated Othon fathered Bari Didi biologically is raised as a question by Lothar but the explanation is cut off before completion.
- The printed page numbers visible in several scans do not match the supplied page labels, suggesting a possible discrepancy between issue-internal numbering and the file sequence.
- The exact identity and nature of the small floating narrator who addresses Tonto are not stated on any page.

Volume: 3

Title: The Knighting of Othon

Chronology:
- FRAMING LAYER — Present: Robots Lothar and Tonto narrate Metabaron ancestry inside the Metabunker while a crisis unfolds on Terra 2014.
- PRESENT ACTION: A Zacuda Frolex (last of its kind) drifts into Terra 2014 through a ventilation hatch, dies in a Police Central computer, and lays one egg; machine shocks mutate the egg into an enormous creature that reactivates an attack program and brings three proto-nuclear units online.
- PRESENT ACTION: The Metabunker comes under organized military assault. Lothar and Tonto race a countdown to reactivate the Metabaron's bio-electrogram. The bald Metabaron manifests briefly, arms the metacraft, defeats three armored opponents in under three seconds, and destroys multiple targets in a timed space combat run before his bio-electrogram dissolves.
- BACKSTORY (recap from prior issues): Othon wins the war on Marmola, loses his wife, defeats enemies with only a dagger, negotiates with the Imperial Couple for a share of epyphite revenues and a new stronghold. Othon and Bari settle on Okhar; Bari loses use of his legs and receives a genetically recreated horse. Thieves steal the horse; Othon pursues them and kills the last bandit, who shoots off Othon's groin and hips. His servants cannot restore his reproductive organs.
- BACKSTORY — Othon's transformation: After mutilation, Othon abandons pure martial training, invests his fortune in early Metabaronic weapons, becomes cruel and solitary, takes Iku-Itta's daughters as enforced-silent companions, and uses an army of machines to transform the Castaka fortress on Okkar into a maxi-protonic tower-city.
- BACKSTORY — Imperial heir crisis: A galaxy-wide broadcast announces the successful fertilization of the empress's ovum with the sterile emperor's sperm after thirty years of effort. Othon immediately recognizes the political danger of pirate abduction.
- BACKSTORY — Janus-Jana revealed: The imperial embryo is conjoined male-female twins joined at neck and shoulders; identified in narration as Janus-Jana, a future galactic empress.
- BACKSTORY — Pirate ambush: The Mother-Coach fortress-ship transports the perfect androgyne to the Golden Planet under purple endoguard escort. Pirate commander Namar launches 100,000 Ostrov-class fighters from a counterfeit planet in the Harp constellation. The battle drags on; the Ekonomat and colonial planets withhold reinforcements.
- BACKSTORY — Othon's intervention: Othon (also called Shazam) regains his voice. The Emperor and Empress broadcast an empire-wide civilian appeal. Othon pilots through the Golden Planet's poly-radars, quantum sensors, and photonic barriers; fights through palace guards; and wins command of fifty remaining endoguard ships from the imperial couple.
- BACKSTORY — Battle resolution: Othon attacks Namar's mega-carrier directly, lures pirates into an asteroid field with a forbidden tri-H torpedo, and detonates FB3 bombs hidden in rock fissures, annihilating the fleet. The counterfeit planet surrenders. Othon joins the Mother-Coach escort, then steals the sacred egg and races to the Golden Planet at hyper-light speed.
- BACKSTORY — Knighting: Othon receives a public triumphal reception. The emperor bestows the hereditary title 'Metabaron' on Othon and his descendants. Privately, Othon is contemptuous of the crowd and grieves that he is 'no longer a man.'
- BACKSTORY — Gift arrives: On Otho, Othon mourns his dead son Bari. An imperial ship delivers a promised gift. Othon shuts himself in his great hall of weapons. Veiled woman Honorata enters and identifies herself as the gift; Othon recognizes her as a Shabda-Oud and presses a blade to her throat. Volume ends unresolved.

Major events:
- The Metabaron manifests via temporary bio-electrogram and defeats multiple armored opponents in timed combat during the Metabunker assault.
- A mutant Zacuda Frolex spawned inside a Police Central computer reactivates an attack program and brings proto-nuclear units online on Terra 2014.
- Pirate commander Namar deploys 100,000 Ostrov-class fighters from a counterfeit planet against the imperial Mother-Coach convoy in the Harp constellation.
- Othon infiltrates the Golden Planet undetected, fights through palace guards, and wins imperial command of fifty endoguard ships.
- Othon destroys the pirate fleet by detonating FB3 bombs in asteroid fissures and forcing the counterfeit planet to surrender.
- Othon steals the sacred egg from the Mother-Coach and flees at hyper-light speed to the Golden Planet.
- The emperor bestows the hereditary title 'Metabaron' on Othon von Salza, founding the dynasty.
- Janus-Jana is revealed as conjoined male-female imperial twins, product of thirty years on a hospital-planet, identified as a future empress.
- Honorata, a Shabda-Oud, arrives as an imperial gift; Othon threatens her with a blade as the volume ends.

Recurring motifs:
- Bodily mutilation as dynastic rupture and personal transformation: Othon's destroyed reproductive organs are the central wound driving the entire arc.
- Timed survival: bio-electrogram countdown, combat timestamps, and battle durations create repeated pressure around finite windows of action.
- The sacred egg as political object: the imperial embryo and the stolen egg are prizes that powerful factions fight to possess or protect.
- Machine vs. organic existence: Lothar and Tonto explicitly contrast robotic endurance with biological decay and grief.
- Betrayal beneath public celebration: Othon despises the crowds honoring him and believes they wanted him to fail.
- Dynastic inheritance under threat: every Metabaron generation is conceived under extreme difficulty or after bodily loss.
- Unstoppable solo intrusion: Othon penetrates planetary defenses alone and is treated as near-invincible by observers.

Lore laws:
- Epyphite is a sacred anti-gravity oil in the heart of planet Marmola; controlling it is worth imperial planetary concessions.
- A bio-electrogram is a temporary solid manifestation of a person's consciousness; it dissolves after roughly three minutes.
